III. THE PROBABLE IMPACT OF THE PROPOSED IMPROVEMENT ON THE ENVIRONMENT
INDIRECT IMPACTS ON THE AREA OR REGION.
The reconstruction and improvement of Lincoln Highway should not have any significant adverse indirect impacts on the area or region in which the roadway is located.
The City of Chicago Heights is located near the southern boundary of Cook County, 25 miles south of the Chicago Loop. It was first established as a community in the early 1800's under the name of "Thorn Grove Settlement." The area had been the home first of the Illini, and then the Pottawatomie Indians, who occupied the high grounds between the Des Plaines and the Kankakee Rivers. In 1833 this area saw the beginning of the urban development which was later to become the City of Chicago Heights.
In 1848, Thorn Grove Settlement had changed its name to "Bloom." This name was used for 45 years until 1893, when the town was incorporated and assumed its present name. This 45 year period was relatively uneventful. The population growth had not been very significant, and industrial development, though started during the Civil War, had not yet achieved the significance that it was to have a few years later.
Industrial expansion in Chicago Heights fundamentally affected the character and pattern of growth of the city's population. Significant industrial activities coincide in fact with significant population expansion. The city's population, which was just over 5,000 people at the turn of the century, nearly tripled between 1900 and 1910. The population was 14,525 in 1910; 19,653 in 1920; and 22,321 in 1930. From 1930 to 1940, the population remained practically unchanged, but after 1940, and up to the present time, the population growth has kept pace with the quickening industrial expansion.
The City of Chicago Heights, Village of Olympia Fields, Village of Park Forest and the Village of Matteson is now, and has been for a number of years, an integral part of the larger Chicago Metropolitan Complex. This metropolitan area is composed of six counties in Illinois with a total area of nearly 4,000 square miles.
